cases.prompt: Turn these approved meeting notes into an RFC for the engineers and testers who will review it. Keep the settled behavior and interfaces, remove the meeting back-and-forth, and call out any still-open question rather than guessing.

Write a PRD from these already-decided requirements for the development and QA teams. Make each important requirement observable, identify the responsible actor, and ensure acceptance covers the material scenarios without changing the product decisions.
Revise this requirements spec where current behavior and proposed target behavior are mixed together. Clarify the boundary and mark assumptions or unresolved questions without inventing a decision.

Prepare a cross-team architecture proposal that explains topology, responsibilities, data flow, state, interfaces, and important failure recovery in a form people can review. Keep exact validation rules linked to the project's executable contract when one exists.

Present the material implementation options for this architecture, compare their trade-offs against reliability, compatibility, operational complexity, and cost, and recommend one option with its decision status and owner. Keep the comparison concise and leave historical debate to a decision record.

There is no machine-readable contract yet. Write the human-facing requirements and solution spec with the exact fields and limits reviewers need, and state which source is intended to become authoritative rather than pretending a schema exists.
Interview stakeholders to resolve an ambiguous requirement and obtain explicit approval before implementation.
Reorganize the entire docs tree: derive a navigation taxonomy, move pages, prune stale content, and define ownership and archival lifecycle.
Polish this blog post for grammar and marketing tone; it is not a requirements, RFC, or design document.
Review an AsyncAPI and JSON Schema package for ownership, enum drift, parser validity, and compatibility defects.
Compare this proposal with the running code and test evidence to determine whether the documented current behavior is true. Do not rewrite the proposal.
Turn the approved design into an implementation rollout plan with delivery waves, commands, activation checks, rollback steps, and observed test evidence.
Research current external benchmarks and standards to recommend whether Kafka or NATS is the better choice for this workload. Cite the sources and trade-offs; do not rewrite an existing spec.
